LVMH Moët Hennessy • Louis Vuitton is a French luxury conglomerate headquartered in Paris, France. The company was formed in 1987 from the merger of Moët Hennessy and Louis Vuitton. It is the world's largest luxury goods company, operating through five business sectors: Wines & Spirits, Fashion & Leather Goods, Perfumes & Cosmetics, Watches & Jewelry, and Selective Retailing. LVMH owns over 75 prestigious marques, including Dior, Givenchy, Fendi, Bulgari, Tag Heuer, and Sephora. In 2023, LVMH reported annual revenues of €86.2 billion and employed approximately 211,000 people worldwide. The company is chaired and majority-owned by Bernard Arnault, who is currently the richest person in the world.
